rows: Maintenance Procedures Information System
Overhead Lines
Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: TL-046-r0a
Equipment: Overhead lines, 220 kV
Issued to: Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company
Status: Approved
Approval date: 27 February 2007
Procedure: Live washing using the American International truck
Next review date: February 2012

This document sets out the procedures for cleaning 220 kV insulators with pressurised water live, using the equipped washing truck. The truck runs on diesel, has 8 cylinders and 140 horsepower, and is fitted with outriggers to rest on during work. Mounted on the truck is a water pressure unit, consisting of a four-stage centrifugal water pump, fitted with pressure control devices and hose connections and water jet nozzles, carried on mechanically operated hydraulic lifts; these lifts can be controlled from inside or outside the truck cabin to reach the correct position. There is also a steel water tank of 1700 gallons (5 m3) capacity. The document was prepared by Eng. Abdel Monem Mohamed Abdel Hadi, and the field test was carried out on 2 December 2006 on the overhead line South El-Tebbin / El-Tebbin 500, 220 kV, and it was approved by Eng. Said Mahmoud El-Sheemy, Head of the Lines Sector, Cairo Electricity Region. The document was approved at session No. 8 on 27 February 2007 of the meeting of sector heads, general managers and those responsible for line maintenance in the regions.

Issue the work order for this before starting work, including the following: - Names of the workers, date, time and place of work, line name and tower number and type; if the work location is very far away, the work supervisor may issue the work order by telephone signal. - The name of every item of equipment at the work location; the resistivity of the water used in washing shall not be less than 1300 ohm/cm, or the conductivity of the water shall not exceed 769 micro-mho (Siemens). No solvents shall be added to the water used in the washing process.
- Wind speed value, water pressure (from 400 to 500 psi).
- Occupational safety and health category of the washers.

The workers must pass an annual examination in live washing, to make sure they fully understand how to use each item of equipment and understand and are able to complete the washing process; this examination shall be recorded in the workers' register and in each person's occupational safety and health card.
An annual medical examination shall be carried out on the workers and recorded in their register.

Make sure there is a permanent and direct means of communication between the work location and the nearest transformer station able to provide communication between the work supervisor and the responsible Control.
Make sure the truck and the hydraulic lifts are sound.
Make sure the truck's portable earth (75 mm2) is connected.
Workers must not touch the equipment or approach it during washing, and must stay away from the wet ground and the earthed equipment at a distance of not less than 2 m.
Safe clearance distances shall be observed as per the attached table.
Carry out the washing steps in exact sequence, without rushing the work or neglecting any step.
Make sure there are no broken discs in the insulators; washing shall not be carried out if the number of broken discs exceeds one third of the total number of discs in the insulator string.
If the water pressure changes, the washing technician shall immediately move the water jet away from the insulator, the conductor and the tower body.

Work must be stopped in the following cases: bad weather such as rain, lightning, thunder, storms or fog, or if the wind speed exceeds 10 m/s, or at nightfall, or when visibility decreases, or upon loss of voltage or disconnection caused by the washing process or for any other reason.
Washing truck equipped for this purpose.
Wind speed measuring instrument.
Water resistance measuring instrument.
Personal protective equipment such as: protective goggles, safety helmet, safety belt, safety shoes, insulating gloves, communication devices, water-absorbent overalls.
Portable earth.
Obtain the approval of the responsible Control for the work.
Issue the work order for this.
The truck is parked under the tower to be washed, between the two circuits, taking into account the wind direction.

Prepare the truck for work: raise the outriggers, taking into account the clearance distances as per the table; raise the boom at an angle of 45 degrees; operate the water pressure pump and make sure of the pressure and length of the water column.

Start washing the first phase, then the second, then the third, from bottom to top, as follows: - Take care to start by washing the circuit in the wind direction within the permitted limits. - Direct the water between the insulator discs, starting from bottom to top, then from top to bottom, then move to the other phase.
After finishing washing the three phases from bottom to top, the middle phase, then the lower phase, must be rinsed of the spray falling from washing the upper phase.
After finishing washing, return the truck to its previous condition so that it can move to another place.

uncertain_terms.note: Tank capacity is given as '1700 gallons (5 m3)' in the source; the two values do not agree (1700 gallons is about 6.4 m3 imperial / 7.7 m3 US). Kept as written.
Line name includes 'التبين 500' rendered as 'El-Tebbin 500'; the '500' is unexplained in the source (the line voltage is 220 kV).
'أفرول لامتصاص المياه' rendered literally as 'water-absorbent overalls'; the parallel documents say 'non-absorbent' overalls, so this is probably a source omission of 'غير قابل'.
'ميكرو موهو "سيمنس"' rendered as 'micro-mho (Siemens)'; the source gives both the old unit (mho) and Siemens.
The clearance table (section 11) contains only the header row; no data rows survive in the source.
Stray '0' at the end of parts of section 6:0:0 and section 6:2:0 looks like an OCR artefact; omitted.
